source.title: Exploring Superposition and Interference in State-of-the-Art Low-Parameter Vision Models
source.authors: Lilian Hollard; Lucas Mohimont; Nathalie Gaveau; Luiz Angelo Steffenel

record.tranche_reason: The study tests architecture-dependent reliance on interference by adding SoLU to convolutional bottlenecks and reporting accuracy and feature-alignment outcomes, using a different method from the original neuron-level analyses.
record.gate_note: The study reports results for SoLU interventions and feature-map alignment. It does not report semantic interpretations of individual neurons or a count/share of polysemantic neurons. ImageNet scaling comparisons for NoDepth are not recorded as rows because the text does not report a numeric or explicit outcome tied to polysemanticity; the feature-alignment statement about NoDepth is recorded below.
record.test_reason: The study inserts SoLU into convolutional bottlenecks and assumes it reduces interference or superposition. It then reports accuracy changes and feature-map alignment (Oij). It never measures whether neurons are polysemantic, or what share are, with or without SoLU. So the accuracy drops cannot show that polysemanticity changes with architecture or can be lowered cheaply (V5). The Oij alignment of feature-map channels is a related but different construct; it is recorded under fits_no_version. The study relies on SoLU as a tool, so it is T4 rather than a test of V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that MobileNetv2/v3 and Batch-Norm MobileNeXt rely on interference and scale poorly at very low parameter counts. They also conclude that ConvNeXt, Layer-Norm MobileNeXt, NoDepth and MobileNetv1 are less affected by SoLU, and that reducing interference dependence improves low-parameter scaling. The NoDepth proof of concept is said to scale better on ImageNet (Figure 11, no numbers given).
record.recipe_differences: The study inserts SoLU into convolutional bottleneck residual streams and examines accuracy and feature-map alignment; it does not reproduce the original neuron-level method. It also compares architecture and normalization variants.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies with bottleneck architecture and normalization: Batch Norm versus Layer Norm, and Inverted, Sandglass, and ConvNeXt-like bottleneck designs.

fits_no_version.finding: SoLU's accuracy cost varies by bottleneck design and normalization. It is nearly 50% for Inverted Bottlenecks and up to 42% with Batch Norm. It is about 1% for ConvNeXt and 4% for Layer-Norm MobileNeXt or Sandglass.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The accuracy cost of inserting SoLU into convolutional bottlenecks depends on architecture and normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature-map channel alignment (Oij) changes under SoLU in MobileNetv3 and Batch-Norm MobileNeXt. In MobileNetv3, features align more closely under SoLU. It stays similar in ConvNeXt, Layer-Norm MobileNeXt and NoDepth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SoLU's effect on feature-map alignment in vision bottlenecks depends on architecture and normalization, and can increase alignment.

record.problems: The reported accuracy differences are mostly percentage drops without absolute accuracy values, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests. CIFAR-10 is the stated primary benchmark; the text provides no numerical NoDepth ImageNet result. Feature-map alignment is used as a proxy for interference, not a direct semantic or neuron-level polysemanticity measure.

untested.parts: No individual neuron is shown responding to unrelated inputs.
Superposition is assumed as the explanation; feature count, sparsity and capacity are not varied.
No sufficient-capacity setting, and no initialization, regularization or noise manipulation.
The share of polysemantic neurons is never measured under any architecture, normalization or SoLU condition. Only accuracy costs of SoLU and feature-map alignment are reported.
No semantic analysis of neuron responses.
No variation of activation range or explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 labels are removed. Accuracy drops under SoLU say nothing about polysemantic-neuron share, because the study never measures polysemanticity. SoLU is assumed to reduce it, yet in MobileNetv3 feature alignment increases under SoLU. No absolute accuracies, uncertainty or statistical tests are reported.

versions.untested_parts: No individual neurons are shown responding to multiple semantic input categories.
No language models, token responses, or transformer MLP neuron rates are studied.
The study does not test whether feature capacity exceeds neuron count, nor vary feature sparsity or capacity pressure.
No sufficient-capacity setting or effects of initialization, regularization, or training noise are tested.

The study examines convolutional bottleneck architectures and SoLU, but does not quantify the share of polysemantic neurons or compare modern convolutional networks broadly. It reports accuracy costs and feature-map alignment, not neuron-level polysemanticity rates.
No semantic analysis tests whether apparently mixed neuron responses share a feature or job.
No activation-range comparison or explanation-scoring method is varied.

rows.subject: Inverted Bottlenecks (MobileNetv2 and MobileNetv3)
rows.operation_detail: Trained bottleneck implementation with SoLU in the residual stream, compared with the base architecture.
rows.measure: Accuracy change when interference is reduced with SoLU
rows.baseline: base architecture accuracy; exact value not stated
rows.note: The text reports the result jointly for MobileNetv2 and MobileNetv3 and does not give model-specific drops.
rows.check: This is an accuracy cost of the SoLU intervention, with no measure of polysemantic-neuron share. It cannot show V5's effect. The value is read from Figure 5 text ('nearly 50%'), jointly for v2 and v3.

rows.subject: ConvNeXt-like Bottleneck (ConvNeXt)
rows.operation_detail: Compared the base architecture with its SoLU implementation.
rows.measure: Accuracy change when interference is reduced with SoLU
rows.baseline: base architecture accuracy; exact value not stated
rows.value: 1% impact; described as having no effect on accuracy
rows.note: The paper describes the result as no effect in Section 4.1 and gives a 1% impact in Section 4.2.
rows.check: This is accuracy only, with no polysemanticity measure. Section 4.1 says 'no effect' for ConvNeXt and Layer-Norm MobileNeXt; Section 4.2 gives 1% for ConvNeXt.

rows.subject: ConvNeXt-like Bottleneck
rows.operation_detail: Tested a standard bottleneck with ReLU and Batch Norm in the ConvNeXt vessel, with SoLU.
rows.baseline: base implementation; exact accuracy not stated
rows.note: The text reports an average across multiple scaling scenarios.
rows.check: This is accuracy only, with no polysemanticity measure. The 6% is an average across scaling scenarios for a ReLU and Batch-Norm bottleneck in the ConvNeXt vessel.

rows.subject: Inverted Bottleneck
rows.operation_detail: Replaced Batch Norm with Layer Norm and tested the bottleneck with SoLU.
rows.baseline: base implementation; exact accuracy not stated
rows.note: The authors state that Layer Norm alone does not account for ConvNeXt's smaller drop.
rows.check: This is accuracy only, with no polysemanticity measure.

rows.subject: Sandglass Bottleneck
rows.operation_detail: Tested the Sandglass Bottleneck with SoLU in the architecture comparison.

conditions.value: Layer Norm in the simulated comparison

rows.baseline: base implementation; exact accuracy not stated
rows.note: The section describes a simulation using Layer Norm in place of traditional Batch Norm.
rows.check: This is accuracy only. It likely reports the same 4% result as R6 (Sandglass with Layer Norm = MobileNeXt with Layer Norm), so it is a possible duplicate row.

rows.subject: MobileNeXt
rows.operation_detail: Replaced Batch Norm with Layer Norm and compared the SoLU and base implementations.
rows.baseline: base model; exact accuracy not stated
rows.note: Section 4.2 explicitly reports this result for MobileNeXt with Layer Norm.
rows.check: This is accuracy only, with no polysemanticity measure. It is possibly a duplicate of R5.

rows.subject: MobileNeXt
rows.operation_detail: Compared the Batch Norm base model with its SoLU implementation.
rows.baseline: base model; exact accuracy not stated
rows.note: The paper contrasts this Batch Norm result with a 4% average drop after replacing Batch Norm with Layer Norm.
rows.check: This is accuracy only, with no polysemanticity measure. The 42% figure is stated for Batch Norm after high-dimensional pointwise expansion and reduction across architectures, and is reiterated for MobileNeXt.

rows.subject: MobileNetv3
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature-map direction alignment in the base model and the model trained with SoLU.
rows.baseline: Base feature maps are described as mostly orthogonal, with Oij values ranging from 0 to 0.5
rows.value: With SoLU, feature directions align more closely
rows.note: This is a feature-map alignment result, not a count or share of polysemantic neurons.

rows.subject: ConvNeXt
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature-map organization with and without SoLU.
rows.baseline: Most features are described as organizing orthogonally
rows.value: The base and SoLU implementations follow the same behavior; slight noise or interference is assumed to align within their own direction space
rows.note: The authors state that the slight-interference interpretation is an assumption; this does not measure neuron-level polysemanticity.

rows.subject: MobileNeXt
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed feature directions in the base model and with SoLU.
rows.measure: Share of layers with feature alignment
rows.baseline: More than 50% of layers exhibit feature alignment in the base model
rows.value: SoLU disrupts the architecture's reliance on this interference-based representation
rows.note: The study reports a layer-level feature organization result, not a polysemantic-neuron share.

rows.subject: MobileNeXt
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature organization in the base model and with SoLU after changing normalization.
rows.baseline: Base model has the reported high-dimensional feature organization; exact measure not stated
rows.value: Similar high-dimensional organization is maintained and SoLU does not significantly disrupt it
rows.note: No numerical measure or neuron-level polysemanticity rate is reported.

rows.subject: NoDepth Bottleneck
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature alignment in the base architecture and its SoLU implementation.
rows.value: Feature alignment remains roughly the same despite interference-noise reduction
rows.note: This is an explicit qualitative alignment result; the text gives no numerical value.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
